llm.summary: The skill's code, requirements, and runtime instructions are consistent with a local browser-extension data-collection tool that talks to a local bridge; nothing in the bundle appears to be trying to do unrelated work or exfiltrate secrets by itself — but it can start arbitrary bridge commands or run over SSH, so exercise caution about what bridge you allow it to run and which remote hosts you target.

dimensions.detail: The skill name/description (web collection via local bridge) matches the included scripts and instructions. Required binaries (curl, node) are appropriate for making HTTP calls to a local bridge and parsing JSON. No unrelated cloud credentials or config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts instruct the agent to start a local bridge, POST to /api/collect, poll /api/tasks/<id>, and wait for final JSON before replying. This stays within the declared purpose. Note: the instructions require Chrome + extension be installed, use the same base URL for all calls, and enforce blocking/synchronous behavior (the agent must wait until the script exits). This grants the agent the ability to run long-lived local commands and spawn the bridge if requested.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or remote downloads are used; the skill is instruction-plus-scripts only. Files are bundled with the skill and will run from disk, so there is no external fetch/execute during install. This is the lower-risk pattern for skills that ship scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not declare or require any secrets or credentials; optional environment variables (used by run.sh) are reasonable for remote execution/bridge configuration. Two things to watch for: (1) the bridge startup is performed by a user-supplied --bridge-cmd (or WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_CMD), which will execute whatever command you provide, and (2) export results may include URLs (export.tableUrl) that point to external locations created by the bridge/exporter. Neither is inherently wrong for this tool, but both are places where sensitive data can leave the machine depending on how the bridge/export is configured.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request permanent inclusion (always:false) and does not try to modify other skills or system-wide configs. It may spawn long-running processes (the bridge) when asked via --ensure-bridge, which is expected for this kind of tool.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent for collecting data via a local browser extension bridge, but before using it: (1) only run it in environments where you trust the bridge binary/command it will start (the --bridge-cmd or WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_CMD will be executed as-is), (2) if you enable remote mode (WEB_COLLECTION_REMOTE_SSH), only point it at SSH hosts you control/trust because it will run commands remotely, (3) review where exported data (export.tableUrl) will be stored or uploaded by the bridge, and (4) be prepared for long-running blocking execution (increase tool timeouts as instructed). If you need stronger guarantees, inspect or run the bridge/connector code in a sandbox before giving the skill live access.
